page.layout: One column of text, centred, with a verse summary at the head, a heading, a short italic passage and then the main paragraph. The left printed page has no margin notes. Part of the facing printed page shows at the right edge; it is not transcribed. Below the text is the catchword.

p.i: Divini ut videant non frivola signa favoris. / Quaeque sit haereticis forma tenenda, monet.

main_text.head: BREVIVS.
CAP. I

p.i: Abste pontifices hi [?] siant argue Cretae. / Sunt bona concta bonis, sunt mala cuncta malis. /
Bis duplicem memorat sexum, piagratia [?] Christi / Nunc tandem apparens, omnia iusta petit. /
Consule parendum, gratis nos Christe vocasti. / Bis monitum fugito, Nicopolimque veni.

main_text.head: Breuissimè.
Declaratio.
main_text.p: Vaniloquis obturandum os:v.10. & Anus sint habi-tu qui sanctimoniam deceat: v.3. Haereticumque fuge post unam & alteram admonitionem:v.10.
main_text.head: ANALYSIS EPISTO-LÆ AD PHILE-monem.
main_text.p: IN paulo-pleniore breuissimæ huius inter Paulinas Epistolæ Analysi, gustum seu specimen extraordinariæ nostræ, in cœtu studiosorum. S. Scripturæ lectionis & considerationis, præbiturus;primo de persona ad quam scribitur, deinde de scripti occasione, tertio de eiusdem pro-positione & summa, quarto de partibus eius quædam delibanda sunt: postea illa quæ ad spe-cialem Analysin Logicam & Theologicam pertinent, breuiter expediam.

page.notes: Right edge: part of the facing printed page (marginal text) is cut off and was left out as the neighbouring page. The small figures "1 2 5" above the italic verse line are uncertain in position and reading. "hi [?] siant" and "piagratia [?]" are doubtful readings. The initial A of the verse summary and the initial I of the paragraph are large decorative letters joined to their words. The long s is set as plain s throughout.
